scenario: Aerospace safety auditors examine only cryogenic fuel storage facilities that maintained active certification. Mean pressure-containment rating (in bar) among audited facilities is 6.3 (σ=1.2); the certification threshold is 4.0 bar. The true mean rating across all facilities commissioned in the programme is sought.

data.description: Observed statistics among units that cleared the survival/publication filter

values.note: Only units above the survival threshold appear in the observed sample

question: (a) Assuming pressure-containment rating is normally distributed with σ=1.2 bar in the full pre-filter cohort, solve numerically for the true pre-filter population mean μ such that E[X | X > 4.0] = 6.3. (b) What fraction of all original units cleared the survival filter? (c) By how much (in bar) does the survivor mean overstate μ? (d) What policy or scientific conclusion error arises from ignoring the survival filter?

ground_truth.explanation: The cryogenic fuel storage facilities in aerospace safety audits dataset is a truncated-normal sample above the survival threshold t=4.0 bar. Solving E[X|X>t]=μ+σφ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ)=6.3 numerically gives μ=6.20907 bar. Only 96.72% of the original cohort survived; the observed mean overstates the true mean by 0.09093 bar. Ignoring the filter leads to over-estimating the baseline quality/capacity of the full cohort, producing over-optimistic policy conclusions.

naive_answer: The true mean pressure-containment rating is 6.3 bar because that is the average observed among the surviving/studied units.
naive_trap: The observed sample consists only of units above the survival threshold. The observed mean is E[X|X>4.0] — a truncated conditional expectation — not the population mean. It systematically overstates μ whenever the threshold is non-trivially binding.
reasoning_trace: (1) Survival filter ≡ truncated-normal sampling with lower truncation at t=4.0. (2) E[X|X>t] = μ + σ·φ((t−μ)/σ) / Φ̄((t−μ)/σ) = 6.3. (3) Solve numerically via brentq on [-26.0, 6.2999] → μ=6.20907. (4) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((4.0−6.20907)/1.2) = 0.96718. (5) Overstatement: 6.3−6.20907 = 0.09093 bar.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 6.3,1.2,4.0
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-25*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=300)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-6.20907)<0.005, f'mu={mu_sol:.5f}'
assert abs(frac-0.96718)<0.005, f'frac={frac:.5f}'
assert mu_sol < obs
assert abs((obs-mu_sol)-0.09093)<0.01
